Everything you mentioned as a Helm feature is not in fact exclusive to Helm, and can be done either in code using the client libraries, or other deployment tools. For example I've written my own deployment tools that provide "value overlays" by simply merging the in-memory structs in Python or Go code - a manifest is just a data structure. I've also written code that can do ordered deployments with checks at multiple stages, which is both easier to do and more powerful when you write Python/Go code than trying to twist your dependencies to fit Helm's sync wave system.
